NORTH AMERICAN P-51D MUSTANG

The fighter this simulator is built around ·

Brief history

North American Aviation designed the NA-73X in 1940 for Britain, and it first flew on 26 October 1940. The early Allison-powered Mustangs were fast down low but weak at altitude. In 1942–43 the Rolls-Royce Merlin engine (built in the US by Packard as the V-1650) turned it into a high-altitude fighter with a laminar-flow wing.

The P-51D, introduced in 1944, added the bubble canopy and six .50-caliber machine guns. With drop tanks it could escort bombers deep into Germany and back, which helped win air superiority over Europe. More than 15,000 Mustangs were built, nearly 8,000 of them P-51Ds. It also served in the Pacific and in Korea, and with air forces around the world into the 1980s. Many still fly today.

How this app compares with the real aircraft

Overall: the airframe is built from our copies of the original factory blueprints and the performance is tuned to the P-51D flight-characteristics manual, as closely as a browser game allows; the low-speed handling, the airspeed placards (stall, flaps, redline), the inverted-flight oil limit and the armament follow the real aircraft closely. By default the app is an arcade-leaning simulation that is fun first: altitude effects, fuel, engine temperatures, spins and engine torque are left out. They are available in the optional Hardcore Simulation Mode (see the Hardcore page, with a master switch and a switch for each part); that page also lists what is still left out. Treat it as a simulation for enjoyment, not a certified model.

The wind speeds, the temperature drop with height and the icing rates are tuned for play, not measured from the aircraft.
How the app figures were measured: level speeds after 90 seconds of level flight at constant throttle, stall speed by slowing at idle until the wing stalls, climb with the nose held at fixed angles (best result quoted), glide with the engine at idle and the nose held at fixed angles until the speed settles, takeoff by running the roll at the real ground attitude. Real figures are the standard published P-51D data and the DCS P-51D flight characteristics manual (flap and airspeed limits, stall table). All of these figures were re-measured for version 4.0 with the method above, by running the game's own physics. Where the standard (arcade) mode differs from the real aircraft, Hardcore mode closes the gap; the Hardcore page lists each part and lets you switch it on or off.

CONTROLS

Three sets: keyboard and mouse, game controller, phone and tablet. The Controls box on screen shows the set for the device you are using (it switches to the controller version when one connects).

Keyboard & mouse

Game controller

Phone & tablet

FullscreenThe flight starts fullscreen, which hides the Android status and navigation bars. Swipe in from the screen edge to show them for a moment. The ⛶ button toggles it, and the pause menu can turn the automatic fullscreen off.
ExitTap the pause button, then Exit game. It leaves fullscreen and closes the app. This works even when the phone’s swipe and Back gestures are hidden by fullscreen.
Hold itSideways (landscape) like a steering wheel works best; portrait works too. Keep the screen upright and facing you: leaning it back a long way makes a twist also nudge the roll. The game calibrates to the way you hold the phone when you start; the target button in the top bar calibrates again.
RollTurn the phone like a steering wheel: clockwise rolls right.
PitchTop edge toward you pulls up; top edge away pushes the nose down (settings can invert it).
RudderTwist the phone left or right, as if turning on the spot. The twist fades after a few seconds, so use the two arrow buttons at the bottom for sustained rudder, for example on the takeoff roll.
ThrottleDrag the slider on the left; drag it to the very top or bottom to snap to full or idle.
ButtonsFIRE (hold), rocket, bomb, gear, brake (hold), flaps up and down. The top bar has the mission menu, pause menu, camera, calibrate, tilt settings and fullscreen.
Without tiltDrag on the right half of the screen as a virtual stick (drag down to pull up). Pinch zooms the camera in or out: it always stays directly behind the plane and never rotates. Double-tap resets the zoom. The camera button switches to the cockpit view.
GraphicsPause menu > Graphics: Auto, Low, Medium or High (N cycles them). Auto picks Low or High and adjusts the resolution to keep the frame rate smooth. Low draws fewer, simpler trees and fewer clouds and no shadow; Medium is in between; High draws everything at full resolution, with detailed branching trees (several kinds of oak and conifer, with textured leaves and needles) around you; to see them, fly to the wooded hill about 4.6 km north-west of the start (heading 323). Close to your own aircraft (Medium and High) it also shows engraved panel lines, rivets, gun barrels, a pitot tube, fuel caps and wheel detail. Near the ground (Medium and High) blade tufts and wild flowers grow around you, fading out about 130 m away. Auto shrinks the zone of detailed trees and grass first, then the resolution, if the frame rate drops. The choice is saved.
Install / offlineWhen the game is served from a web address (for example GitHub Pages) the browser can install it as an app (Add to Home Screen or Install) and it then runs full screen and offline.
Hardcore modePause menu > Hardcore: a master switch and a switch for each real-aircraft detail (torque, spins, altitude, engine temperature, fuel, war emergency power, load limits, ILS realism, wind, turbulence, wet runway, icing). Off by default.
LayoutSwipe any instrument box off the screen to hide it. The pause menu has a checkbox for everything you can show or hide, and Move boxes lets you drag the boxes and buttons where you want them. Your choices are remembered, separately for landscape and portrait.
TipsiPhone and iPad ask permission for motion sensors the first time. If the page is shown inside another page the browser may block the sensors: open it in its own tab. Use Add to Home Screen for a full-screen app.

HARDCORE SIMULATION

Real-aircraft detail for pilots who want it. Off by default: the simulator is fun first.

Hardcore mode adds the things the real P-51D does that an arcade flight model leaves out. Switch it on here, then keep only the parts you enjoy. Each part has its own switch, so you can, for example, fly with spins and torque but ignore fuel and engine temperature. With the master switch off, none of this affects the game and the gauges stay quiet. The settings are saved.

What it models

Torque, P-factor, propwashOn the ground the nose swings left under power; in the air the plane rolls and yaws left at low speed and high power.
Stalls and spinsSPIN warning on the screen. Opposite rudder + stick forward recovers.
AtmosphereStandard-atmosphere density and speed of sound, a two-stage-supercharger power curve, indicated airspeed on every gauge, a lower redline up high, and the same thin air for the bandits.
EngineOverheat after about 4 minutes above 90% throttle (sooner when slow); cools in well under a minute at lower power.
PerformanceSea-level top speed about 600 km/h, about 703 km/h true speed at 7,600 m, cruise about 475 km/h at sea level and about 580–600 km/h near 5,000 m, climb about 15–16 m/s.
Load limits+8 / −4 G at 8,000 lb, scaled down with weight, 15% less at high speed; OVERSTRESS warning, lasting damage, and wing failure at 1.5 times the limit.
Fuel269 US gallon internal tanks, the fuselage tank burned first. FUEL readout on the HUD, LOW FUEL and OUT OF FUEL warnings.
Not modelledDrop tanks, carburetor icing, and gun-recoil or ordnance effects on balance.

OPERATIONS

Missions, cockpit warnings, weapons and enemy difficulty

Missions & trainers (the Missions tab, or press M)

Free flightFly anywhere. A convoy runs on the road every few minutes, with ground targets scattered about. No guide path. Convoy messages only appear on the convoy mission.
Takeoff trainerSeven coached steps from the runway to a safe climb. A path along the centerline and up the climb-out shows where to be. Your liftoff speed is scored at the end.
Landing trainerYou start on the downwind leg of the circuit and must slow down, lower gear and flaps, turn base and final, fly the glide slope, flare and brake. Scored for sink rate, speed and centerline.
Dogfight trainerShoot down 3 bandits. The coach gives the bandit's clock position, range and relative height, and says whether you are attacking or defending. Hull heals and ammunition resupplies between kills.
Convoy strafingOne convoy at a time drives from the depot to the base: a jeep, supply trucks, a tanker and an APC. A path leads you in behind the rear vehicle and follows the road; fire from about 500 m and pull up after the front vehicle. Tankers explode and damage vehicles near them.
Building bombingDestroy the 11 depot and base buildings. A path takes you level at 900 m, then into a 25° dive. The red IMPACT circle shows where a bomb would land; the coach says GET READY and then RELEASE NOW. Ordnance resupplies a few seconds after you use it all.
Barrel rollPull the nose up, then corkscrew around an imaginary barrel ahead with a steady roll and a light pull the whole way. Scored for heading error, height change and keeping the G above zero. Hardcore mode: enter faster and use rudder for the torque.
Immelmann turnHalf loop up, then a half roll to level: you leave heading the other way and higher. Standard mode: about 520 km/h and 3.5 to 4.5 G. Hardcore mode: about 650 km/h, 4.5 to 5.5 G, right rudder as the speed bleeds off, and watch the stall at the top.
Split SRoll onto your back and pull through a half loop down: the fastest way to reverse course and lose height. Start 2,400 m up with the throttle closed; it needs about 1,000 m. Hardcore mode: watch the speed and the G limit.
WingoverA climbing turn that trades speed for height, a pause with the nose falling through the horizon, then a diving turn back to your start height on the reverse heading.
Low yo-yoAgainst a scripted drone that turns left and never fires: you are in lag behind his turn, so dive below him to gain speed, cut across, then zoom up onto his tail inside 450 m without overshooting. Hardcore mode: you lose energy faster, so keep full power.
High yo-yoThe drone is slower than you: you would overshoot, so pull up out of his turn plane, trade the speed for height, then roll over and drop behind him. Hardcore mode: pull up smoothly and keep the speed above 250 km/h.

Takeoff

  1. Flaps 10° (F once). Gear stays down.
  2. Full power. Keep her straight on the centerline: roll input steers on the ground.
  3. Rotate at about 160 km/h: ease the stick back until the nose is about 10° above the horizon and hold it.
  4. Liftoff at 170–180 km/h, 17–20 seconds after you start rolling. Then gear up.
  5. Hold the nose 8–10° up while the speed builds to 240 km/h, then flaps up.
  6. Climb out at about 250 km/h.

Landing

  1. Fly the circuit: downwind, a right turn onto base about 1.5 km past the threshold, a second right turn onto final.
  2. Idle early: 340 to 210 km/h takes about 20 seconds. Gear below 350 km/h, then flaps 10°, 20°.
  3. Final at 210 km/h on a 3° glide slope. Nose for speed, throttle for height.
  4. Too fast? Idle, nose up a little, flaps 20°. Still over 260 km/h inside 1 km: go around.
  5. Flare about 8 m up: idle, nose to about 8°. Touch down at 160–180 km/h, sink under 3 m/s, then brakes.
  6. Stop with the throttle at idle: repairs and rearms in about 4 seconds.
You crash with a sink rate over about 7 m/s, gear up, steeply tilted, or leaving the runway faster than about 70 km/h.

Flight path guide (trainers)

A glowing path leads you in: green is the curve to fly now, gold is the final line. On the screen, steer the white flight-path marker (it shows where the plane is really going) into the green STEER HERE ring. The gold ring is only your gun aiming point. The path stays fixed in the world, is planned for a gentle 30–38° bank at 360 km/h or faster, and uses dive and glide angles the P-51 can fly. The coach panel lists how far off the path you are. L hides or shows it; K shrinks the coach panel to one line.

Cockpit warnings

STALLThe wing is stalled. Release the stick, lower the nose, add power. The STALL readout on the left panel shakes within a few km/h of the stall.
PULL UPLow and descending fast.
ILSThe landing trainer teaches the instrument landing system. The ILS panel (beside the artificial horizon) is a cross-pointer: the vertical needle is the localizer (left / right of the runway centreline) and the horizontal needle is the glide slope (your height against a 3° slope that meets the runway 200 m past the threshold). Each needle points toward where the beam is, so fly toward the needle: needle right = turn right, needle below the centre = descend. Red LOC / GS flags mean no beam yet. The beam reaches about 25 km out and 40° either side of the runway, for both ends (36 and 18; in free flight the nearer end is used, switched on with L). The distance (DME) to the threshold is shown at the top. Standard needles are full scale at 5° and 1.4°. In the landing trainer the green ring leads you around the circuit and then sits on the centreline and the slope. Catch the slope from below. Hardcore > ILS realism uses the real sensitivity (2.5° and 0.7°), a narrower cone, the outer and middle marker beacons with lamps and tones, and capture call-outs.
Photo modePause menu > Photo mode, or F9. The game freezes and you get a free camera: W A S D move, Q / E down and up, Z / C roll, drag the mouse to look, the right-drag slides the camera, the wheel moves it in and out in small steps (Shift + wheel in big steps; it never runs out), Ctrl + wheel changes the field of view, Shift moves fast. The panel sets the field of view, the time of day and the weather (these revert when you leave), the picture size (up to 4K), the JPG quality, and whether the HUD boxes and your aircraft are shown. “Stamp info” prints the version, date, mode, position, speed, game time and weather on the photo, which helps when reporting a problem. Enter or Space takes the photo and your browser saves the JPG. H switches the HUD, F hides the panel, Esc leaves. “Action: running” lets the flight continue while you move the camera.
Time & weatherSettings > Time of day & weather. Time: your local clock, dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, evening or night; tick “Time passes” to run a day in 24 minutes. Weather: clear, partly cloudy, overcast, rain, thunderstorm or fog. Overcast, rain, storm and fog cut how far you can see and dim the sun. At night you get a moon, stars, runway lights, lit building windows, the hangars and the tower, and wingtip and tail lights (red left, green right, white tail). Rain streaks past the canopy; a thunderstorm adds lightning and thunder. Fly the runway lights in, and watch your altitude. Night: the instrument panel dims, and with the landing gear down the landing light puts a pool of light on the ground ahead of the nose.
DAMAGEEnemy hits hurt one system at a time (Settings > Battle damage). Engine: less power, smoke, then fire or a dead engine. Wing: the plane rolls toward the damaged side and the aileron weakens (lost when badly hit). Tail: weaker elevator and rudder. Fuel tank: a leak. Hydraulics: flaps jam and the gear will not retract. A fire burns the hull: dive fast for about 3 seconds to put it out. Land and stop with the throttle at idle to repair everything. If it is hopeless, bail out (J twice, or hold both bumpers, or Pause menu > Bail out): the canopy blows off, you climb out of the seat, fall clear and the parachute opens. Drag the mouse (or use the right stick) to look all around, down at the ground and up at the canopy. You need about 100 m of height when you climb out for the parachute to open in time; Enter restarts at any time. The aircraft is lost.
SoundThe engine note follows the throttle and propeller speed, with wind, tyre rumble, guns, rockets, bombs and explosions (heard late when far away), and a chirp and squeal of rubber when you touch down fast. Warning tones: a pulsing buzzer for a stall, a steady wail past the redline, a two-tone warble in a spin, and fast beeps for overstress. Settings > Sound has the overall volume and a separate Engine & Wind volume; U mutes.
OVERSTRESS (Hardcore)You are pulling more G than the airframe is rated for. Ease off at once: the damage adds up, and about 1.5 times the limit breaks the wing. Landing and stopping at idle repairs it.
SPIN (Hardcore)The aircraft is spinning. Opposite rudder and the stick forward; throttle back. Then pull out gently.
ENGINE OVERHEAT (Hardcore)Too long above 90% throttle. Reduce power until the temperature falls. The oil and coolant gauges and the HUD TEMP readout show it.
LOW FUEL / OUT OF FUEL (Hardcore)Land soon. With no fuel the engine stops: glide to a landing. Landing and stopping at idle refuels you.
ICING (Hardcore)Ice is building on the wing in cloud below freezing. Leave the cloud or descend to warmer air (the HUD shows the outside temperature and the ice). It cuts lift and thrust and adds drag; the cockpit frosts over.
WIND, GUSTS, TURBULENCE (Hardcore)The HUD WIND line shows where the wind blows from, its speed, and the head or tail and the left or right cross component for the way you are pointing. Crab into a crosswind in the air; on the ground use rudder against the tail wheel's weathercock. The windsock by the tower shows the surface wind. The ILS picks the runway end into the wind. In rough air ease the controls and slow down.
WET RUNWAY (Hardcore)After rain the brakes are weaker and the steering is weak; above about 160 km/h in heavy rain the aircraft hydroplanes and the brakes hardly work. Touch down early and brake gently.
REDLINE – COMPRESSIBILITYOver about 755 km/h: buffet and stick jitter. Ease off.
G LIMITPulling more than about 6.5 G. Above about 4.5 G sustained the screen greys out and you black out.
OIL PRESSUREInverted for more than 10 seconds cuts the engine. Roll upright to recover.
Flaps overspeedFlaps retract on their own if you exceed their speed limit (10° 640, 20° 440, 30°/45° 360 km/h). In Hardcore mode the flaps have the real six settings: 10° 644, 20° 443, 30° 362, 40° 290, 50° 265 km/h.
Gear overspeed (Hardcore)The gear will not come down above 273 km/h (170 mph): the HUD says GEAR OVERSPEED. Slow down and try again.
WAR EMERGENCY / RPM (Hardcore)More than 5 minutes above 90% throttle, or more than 3 seconds above 3240 rpm in a fast dive, overheats the engine. Throttle back and let it cool.
Panel lampsGEAR is green with the gear down. FLAPS is amber when flaps are out. STALL is amber near the stall. ENG FAIL is red when the engine has cut. MAGS, BATT, CANOPY and INVERTER are always green.
Coach colorsGreen: on target. Amber: adjust. Red: danger.

Weapons

GunsSix .50 cal (12.7 mm), 1,840 rounds: 380 on each inboard gun, 270 on the other four. About 800 rounds a minute each, muzzle speed 880 m/s. Bullets drop under gravity. The gold ring is where they converge, about 350 m ahead; the orange ring shows where to aim to lead a bandit.
RocketsSix 127 mm HVAR, fired in order from the rails, leaving 60 m/s faster than you with no guidance. Fire from 800–1,000 m with the gold ring on the target.
BombsTwo 230 kg (500 lb), released with Z / X / the BOMB button. A bomb keeps your speed and falls for about 5 seconds. The blast reaches 75 m and does less damage with distance.
WeightBombs and rockets add weight and raise the stall speed; it drops as you use them.
ResupplyLand and stop with the throttle at idle: about 4 seconds to repair, rearm and (in Hardcore mode) refuel. The trainers also top up ammunition and hull for you.
TargetsThe compass shows the nearest target in red (T), home in white (H) and the nearest bandit in pink (B). Fuel tanks and tankers explode. Hull damage from enemy hits shows on the left panel.

Choose the skill with the buttons on the start screen, keys 1 / 2 / 3, or a tap of R3 on a controller. One bandit appears at a time (in the air, B or the controller B button calls one, and pressing it again clears it). The bandit flies by the same physics as you: it stalls if it pulls too hard, loses speed and height in hard turns, and crashes if it hits the ground. Make it keep turning, then get on its tail. Roughly one shot-down bandit in three (when it is high enough) has its pilot bail out: watch for the parachute.
